long_biography.plain_text:
At 24, Gary Klesch became a partner at US investment bank McDonald & Company, giving him unusually early authority in capital markets. A subsequent federal post placed him inside negotiations over loans to distressed businesses, before he moved to Europe to lead Dean Witter Reynolds' regional operation.

In 1990 he created the Klesch Group around a disciplined form of principal investing: buying non-core industrial businesses that were underperforming but retained sound fundamentals. Each acquired operation becomes central to the group's performance. Financial restructuring is paired with direct operating control, commodity-risk management and capital investment in production systems.
long_biography.html:
At 24, Gary Klesch became a partner at US investment bank McDonald & Company, giving him unusually early authority in capital markets. A subsequent federal post placed him inside negotiations over loans to distressed businesses, before he moved to Europe to lead Dean Witter Reynolds' regional operation.

In 1990 he created the Klesch Group around a disciplined form of principal investing: buying non-core industrial businesses that were underperforming but retained sound fundamentals. Each acquired operation becomes central to the group's performance. Financial restructuring is paired with direct operating control, commodity-risk management and capital investment in production systems.
